media.title: Miss Annabelle Lee — video reference, Polydor recording
media.description: This is a popular American song from 1927, written by Sidney Clare, Lew Pollack, and Harry Richman. The piece is an example of 'Tin Pan Alley,' representing the popular music of the Roaring Twenties.
media.altText: Listening reference for “Miss Annabelle Lee”; the video image shows the Polydor record label.
media.rightsNote: External media is linked for scholarly reference and is not rehosted; reuse rights are not cleared.
media.publicCaption: Canonical listening reference for “Miss Annabelle Lee” (Polydor 21768, 1928), performed by Hermann Bick and Dr. Kaper on two pianos. The YouTube video uses the record label as its visual frame.

timelineEvents.title: Jazz Piano Partnership
timelineEvents.label: 1928 · Jazz piano partnership
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper records jazz-influenced piano-duo arrangements with Hermann Biek, credited on the recordings as Hermann Bick, for Polydor.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Together with pianist Hermann Biek, credited on recordings as Hermann Bick, Kaper records two-piano arrangements for Deutsche Grammophon/Polydor. The documented repertoire includes American popular songs such as “Miss Annabelle Lee” and “The Song Is Ended.”
